overall: The AG found the Rehoboth Board of Selectmen violated the Open Meeting Law by posting insufficiently specific notices and failing to timely approve minutes, ordering compliance and member webinar training.

allegations.summary: The June 7 notice listed only 'Reserve Fund Transfer' without detail on the single transfer for tree pruning.
allegations.key_passage: The Board concedes, and we agree, that the Board should have included more detail for this item, as the chair anticipated discussing only a single reserve fund transfer authorizing the payment of $6,730 for tree pruning to be completed by Lewis Tree Service.

allegations.summary: The June 1 notice item 'Approve Board of Health Agent's Contract' allegedly lacked the contract's details.
allegations.key_passage: was sufficiently specific as it reasonably advised the public of the issues to be discussed at the meeting.

allegations.summary: Generic appointment, resignation and license items on several notices did not list the names of the individuals to be considered.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore conclude that the meeting May 24, June 7, June 14 and June 21 notices should have included the names of the individuals to be considered by the Board.

allegations.summary: The Sept. 27 and Oct. 4 notices said documents would be attached, but none were attached.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body attach any documents to the meeting notice, and therefore we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The June 1 notice cited only 'MGL CHAPTER 30A, §21' as the executive session topic, without stating a purpose.
allegations.key_passage: A general citation to the section of the Open Meeting Law which lists all ten permissible purposes for convening in executive session is clearly inadequate.

allegations.summary: The Board failed to approve minutes for about twelve meetings from December 2020 to May 2021 within the required timeframe.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely create and approve meeting minutes.

remedy: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
We order all members of the Board to attend an Open Meeting Law webinar training provided by our office within ninety (90) days of the Board’s receipt of this letter.
We also order the Board to certify to our office that each Board member has completed the webinar training within ninety-five (95) days of the Board’s receipt of this letter.
